thread:
Incident Bot: [ALERT] high 5xx rate for service=redwood-api region=eu on geo-dns routing; automated round-robin fallback triggered (count=3)
Incident Bot: Pager sent to #incidents-oncall and alice.nguyen@pagerduty; priority=P1
Alice Nguyen: acked, looking. seeing spike ~ 11:03 UTC, 5xx across eu-west edge cluster. diffs look like sudden routing to old edge hosts?
Ben King: also seeing increased DNS NX/timeout from Cloudflare resolvers in some regions. random resolvers returning stale answers. dig from GCE eu-west-1 shows:```
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> @1.1.1.1 api.redwood.example A +short +tries=1 +time=2
93.184.216.34
93.184.216.35
```
Ben King: but our canonical Route53 records should be 52.14.23.7 (eu primary), 34.102.45.9 (global fallback) — so resolvers returning 93.184... looks like an expired cached record from a previous demo zone? odd.
Carol Smith: routing mismatch plausibly caused by TTL oscillation after yesterday's test deploy that briefly set very short TTLs then restored. maybe some resolvers cached the old CNAME chain.
Dave O'Connell: customer impact: reports of increased latency and 502s for EU customers on the dashboard. Support ticket surge noted (10 tickets in last 20m).
Maya Rao (Support Lead): pushing a templated update to affected customers ASAP. summary + ETA requested.
Alice Nguyen: mitigation plan: 1) Pause any recent geodns config rollouts (I did that at 11:08). 2) Force a Route53 change to re-emit correct records with low TTL and a new serial to nudge resolvers. 3) Add a temporary geo-fallback in our edge LB to accept traffic for the stale IPs and proxy to correct backend to avoid 5xx.
Ben King: preparing Route53 change now. patch:```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z12345678 --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood.example","Type":"A","TTL":60,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"52.14.23.7"},{"Value":"34.102.45.9"}]}}]}'
```
Alice Nguyen: concurrently I'm opening firewall ACL to accept 93.184.216.0/24 to our eu-edge proxy and routing it to the app pool so we can avoid failing connections while DNS propagates. will watch error rates.
Incident Bot: change request created: CR-9034 by Ben King; status=INSUBMIT
Ben King: change applied to Route53 at 11:12 UTC. propagation check: performing repeated dig from multiple resolvers (1.1.1.1, 8.8.8.8, local isp).
Carol Smith: telemetry shows 5xx rates dropping by 40% after firewall ACL open + route53 change, but some resolvers still returning stale IP (93.184...) — those will TTL-expire shortly as we forced TTL down to 60s.
Alice Nguyen: initiating gradable rollback of the demo zone (yesterday's) to fully remove conflicting CNAMEs; created ticket with DNS-Infra.
Ben King: probes:```
# sample probe results 11:20 UTC
1.1.1.1 -> 52.14.23.7
8.8.8.8 -> 52.14.23.7
ISP-xyz -> 93.184.216.34 (still stale)
```
Dave O'Connell: updated incident page: https://status.redwood.example/incident/2365120000 (note: internal) — customers updated at 11:25 UTC: short post about regional DNS disruption with mitigation in progress.
Maya Rao (Support Lead): posted customer message and set next update for 11:45 UTC. field teams told to triage escalations.
Alice Nguyen: handing off primary on-call to Ben for the next 2h (need to jump to an on-site meeting). Ben, you are IC. I will remain reachable for escalations.
Ben King: taking IC, thanks. summary of current: Route53 records corrected, TTL lowered to 60, temporary ACL to accept stale IPs, demo zone rollback in progress. current impact: degraded for a subset of EU ISPs but overall 5xx rate trending down.
Carol Smith: suggested longer-term actions: 1) Add automated TTL dampening in our GeoDNS controller to prevent bouncing TTLs on quick rollouts. 2) Add resolver health checks and prefer TLS/DOH resolvers for critical entries. 3) Postmortem and DNS playbook update.
Ben King: agreed, will own action items in follow-up.
Incident Bot: escalated to SRE manager at 11:30 UTC due to P1 duration > 15m
Maya Rao (Support Lead): customer comms scheduled and one critical customer (ACME Corp) notified via account team.
Alice Nguyen: leaving note: handoff_complete=true; expected follow-ups: DNS-Infra ticket, postmortem, customer RCA. good job team. :thumbsup:
Ben King: monitoring for another 30m and will update when we mark resolved.
Carol Smith: adding to postmortem board.
---
11:48 UTC Ben King: 5xx nearly back to baseline, ISP caches mostly refreshed. marking incident as mitigated; will keep P1 page open until full resolution and ticket closure.
11:59 UTC Ben King: closing primary mitigations; will convert to P2 for postmortem work.
12:10 UTC Incident Bot: incident state updated -> MITIGATED.
12:15 UTC Maya Rao (Support Lead): final customer update posted: root cause = conflicting demo DNS entries + uneven resolver cache state after TTL change; mitigation = forced Route53 rewrite, lowered TTL, temporary ACL. RCA/PM to follow.
